item.title: [7.0] Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

We present Kandinsky 6.0 Video, a family of foundation diffusion models for synchronized text-to-audio-video generation, comprising Kandinsky 6.0 Video Lite (3B parameters) and Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro (29B parameters). Both models generate 5-second video clips with synchronized 44 kHz audio, including lip-sync, in text-to-audio-video (T2AV) and image-to-audio-video (I2AV) modes; a built-in...

WHY IT MATTERS

item.title: [6.9] OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Recent advances have enabled unified omni-modal models in understanding audio, vision, and language. However, existing benchmarks, training data, and learning methods largely treat the modalities independently, leaving the capability of audio-visual joint reasoning poorly evaluated and insufficiently elicited. We address this gap with a benchmark, data engine, and learning method.

WHY IT MATTERS

This paper addresses a notable gap in multimodal AI by introducing a dedicated benchmark and training pipeline specifically for audio-visual joint reasoning rather than treating modalities independently.

item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Large language models (LLMs) are highly sensitive to the prompts used to specify task objectives and behavioral constraints. Many recent prompt optimization methods iteratively rewrite prompts using LLM-generated feedback, but the resulting prompts often become longer, accumulate narrow sample-specific rules, and generalize poorly beyond the training distribution. We study this failure mode as...

WHY IT MATTERS

TextReg addresses prompt distributional overfitting in automated prompt optimization by introducing a principled regularization framework for discrete text-space optimization.

item.description:

Despite growing interest in this setting for image data, no benchmark exists for time series, which are more challenging. We present the first SF-UniDA benchmark on time series.
